name: Social Isolation Allostatic Load
short_description: Perceived social isolation (loneliness) activates conserved neuroendocrine threat response: HPA dysregulation, elevated cortisol, chronic inflammation, genomic shift (CTRA); mortality risk equivalent to 15 cigarettes/day
higher_order_principle: Perceived social isolation (loneliness) activates a conserved neuroendocrine threat response: HPA axis dysregulation, elevated cortisol, chronic low-grade inflammation, and a genomic shift (CTRA) toward pro-inflammatory gene expression. Architecturally relevant because building designs that reduce chance encounters and social opportunities produce measurable isolation effects. Effect magnitude comparable to major physical stressors.

neuroendocrine_cascade.onset_threshold: ~2 weeks sustained minimal social contact for detectable shift

scope_conditions: Perceived isolation, not objective aloneness, is the trigger — introverts in voluntary solitude are NOT affected
Chronic, not acute: brief periods of solitude are restorative (see ART). Effect requires sustained perceived isolation
Modulated by quality of existing relationships: one deep relationship can buffer against many absent ones
Cultural variation: collectivist cultures may show stronger isolation effects than individualist cultures
Age-dependent: elderly and adolescent populations are most vulnerable
moderators: existing_relationship_quality (one secure attachment substantially reduces risk)
duration (weeks → months → years: escalating and increasingly irreversible)

interactions.nature: T50 uses same HPA axis pathway as T5 (physical threat). Social isolation processed by brain as threat — 'social pain' activates dorsal ACC and anterior insula, overlapping with physical pain circuits.
T50 provides social input channel to allostatic computation. T29 computes allostatic load from sensory and metabolic inputs; T50 adds social isolation as first-class input.
